(b) Fix the positive numerical constant $c$ and, in each inertial chart, define the component families $\\varepsilon_x:=T^{00}$, $\\pi_x^i:=T^{0i}/c=T^{i0}/c$ and $S_x^{ij}:=T^{ij}$. These are numerical component and scaling conventions; their transformation is inherited from $T$. No physical units or measurement interpretation form part of this mathematical definition. (c) When $k\\ge1$, the \\emph{four-force density} of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field with inertial components $f^b:=\\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. By [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\\,(iv) the components $\\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\\Omega$, independent of the inertial chart. For $k\\ge1$, one says that $T$ is \\emph{locally conserved}, or \\emph{balanced}, on $\\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\\Omega$, and that $T$ is balanced against the four-force density $f$ when $\\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$. (d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used.         "statement": "Two exact boundary checks. (i) Stationarity is first order.
